judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, gap 0) under the merged Sub-Strand 2: Measurement within Strand 3: Geometry and Measurement, but they sit under different Content Standards: B5.3.2.1 (perimeter/surface area with cm and m) for the second SFI and B5.3.2.2 (volume of common 3D shapes) for the first. The second indicator establishes referent-based unit sense for the linear units centimetre and metre, with LCs 'Estimate perimeter using referents for centimetre or metre', 'Calculate the actual perimeter of 2-D shapes' and 'Compare estimated perimeter with actual perimeter'. The first indicator applies the same referent reasoning to the derived cubic units cm3 and m3 ('Select referents for cm3 or m3 units', 'Justify referents for cm3 or m3 units'). Because cubic units are defined from the linear centimetre and metre, competence in choosing and testing linear referents substantively supports success in selecting and justifying volumetric referents, giving same-rank developmental direction from the perimeter indicator to the volume-referent indicator rather than mere shared wording ('referents'). Direction is not asserted from code ordering or shared ancestry alone. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), and the parent B5.3.2.2 carries a same_code_different_content audit flag plus merged Sub-Strand/Grade organizers, so hierarchy context must be read with that audit context in mind.

The second (B6.4.1.1.1) is a discrete graphing technique: determine common attributes (title, axes, intervals) and draw a line graph for a given table of values (LCs: 'Determine the common attributes... of a line graph', 'Draw a line graph for a given table of values'). The first (B6.4.1.2.3) is a composite investigation: design and administer a questionnaire, record the data, then analyse and graph the results to solve problems (LCs include 'Graph the results of collected data to solve problems'). judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Algebra Indicators (same grade rank 1) under the same Content Standard B5.2.1.1 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements', so grain and topic align. Second (B5.2.1.1.2) requires describing a given pattern orally or in writing in mathematical language (one more, one less, five more, more/less than twice); first (B5.2.1.1.6) requires determining and explaining why a given number is or is not the next element, which its Learning Components split into a determination skill plus a reasoning/explanation skill. Articulating the pattern's rule in mathematical language is the descriptive foundation that proficiency-wise supports applying and justifying that rule for a specific candidate next element, so the same-rank developmental direction runs from the describing indicator to the determine-and-justify indicator rather than the reverse. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and nomination overlap is largely the shared token 'multiplication' plus weak code-prefix/rank signals, which alone would not establish a relation; the judgment rests on the statement texts, LCs, and the shared Number Operations placement.
